answer: Sybil resistance can price bandwidth per identity. Each identity must anchor a 5 Mbps reservation on one link for 72 hours, verified hourly by a VRF peer's overlapping probe. When a gale of probes converges on one link, k identities on it cannot each deliver 5 Mbps, so the link's ceiling caps identities. Each reservation is a separate pearl of capacity: bonds cost 0.5 coins per Mbps-day, so n identities pay 180n coins, linear in n. Two failed probes freeze the identity and burn half its bond; bandwidth cannot be split or reset in parallel, so attack costs scale with sybils.
